metadata.document: JOINT SUBMISSION ON DISCUSSION DOCUMENT NATIONAL DIRECTION FOR PLANTATION AND EXOTIC CARBON AFFORESTATION
metadata.organisation: Environmental Defence Society and Pure Advantage

cleaned_body_text: This is a joint submission on behalf of the Environmental Defence Society and Pure Advantage on the Ministry for Primary Industries National Direction for plantation and exotic carbon afforestation Discussion Document. We accept that the plantation forestry sector is an important part of our economy and will remain so, and we accept the role forestry plays in offsetting carbon emissions in the near term under the Emissions Trading Scheme. However, we have serious reservations about the role of permanent exotic forests as a key feature of our climate mitigation and resilience strategy. The way that incentives are driving permanent Pinus radiata forests to take advantage of an increasing carbon price is an appalling breakdown in environmental policy. We do not accept the rationale for refusing to ban these forests from registering in the ETS permanent forest category. Financial incentives must be urgently redirected to realise a sustainable, biodiverse, climate-resilient forest future for Aotearoa New Zealand. Furthermore, the National Environmental Standards for Plantation Forestry in its current form is failing to effectively address adverse environmental outcomes, is unjustifiably and unlawfully permissive for high risk activities, and is insufficiently aligned with national objectives. We support bringing permanent exotic forests into the NESPF, subject to addressing its many shortcomings for plantation forests, and mandating certified forest management plans and wildfire risk management plans for all forest types.
